title: A stack in an array
summary: One int, top, says where the top of the stack is. Push moves it up, pop moves it down.

checkpoints.text: The stack is an array of 4 cells and an int `top`. `top` is -1, just left of cell 0: the stack is empty.
`++top` moves `top` to cell 0 first, then 10 is stored there.
Four pushes later the array is full and `top` is 3, the last cell.

checkpoints.at: cout << "Stack overflow: " << value << " does not fit" << endl;
checkpoints.text: Pushing 50: `isFull()` is true, so the push stops here. A fixed-size array can overflow; a linked stack only stops when memory runs out.
Pop returns the value at `top` (40) and then moves `top` down. The 40 is still in the cell, but it is no longer part of the stack: the next push will overwrite it.
Popped 40, then 30: last in, first out. Push and pop each touch one cell and one int, so both are O(1).
